en: (Here begins the second half of the Vriddha Chanakya.) A person without money is not truly poor; he may well be rich. But one who lacks the jewel of learning is poor in every way.
Place your foot where your eyes have checked, drink water strained through cloth, speak words checked against the scriptures, and do what your mind has judged to be pure.
If you want comfort, give up learning; if you want learning, give up comfort. How can one who seeks comfort gain learning, and how can a student have comfort?

first: कवयः किं न पश्यन्ति कि न कुर्वन्ति योषितः ।
en: What can poets not see? What can women not do? What will drunkards not babble? What will crows not eat?
Fate makes a beggar a king and a king a beggar; it makes the rich poor and the poor rich.
A beggar is the enemy of the greedy, a teacher is the enemy of fools, a husband is the enemy of an unfaithful wife, and the moon is the enemy of thieves.

first: येषां न विद्या न तपो न दानं
en: Those who have no learning, no self-discipline, no generosity, no good conduct, no virtue and no righteousness are a burden on the earth; they are beasts walking about in human form.
Advice does not take root in people who are empty inside; bamboo does not become sandalwood just by growing near the Malaya mountain.

first: यस्य नास्ति स्वयं प्रज्ञा शास्त्रं तस्य करोति किम् ।
en: What can scriptures do for one who has no sense of his own? What use is a mirror to one who has no eyes?

first: दुर्जनं सज्जनं कर्तुमुपायो न हि भूतले ।
en: There is no way on earth to make a wicked person good; even if you wash the lower end of the body a hundred times, it does not become a noble part.
Hating those close to you brings death, hating others brings loss of wealth, hating the king brings ruin, and hating the learned destroys the family.

It is better to live in a forest full of tigers and elephants, in the shelter of a tree, living on ripe fruit and water, sleeping on grass and wearing torn bark, than to live poor among one's relatives.

A Brahmin is like a tree: his daily prayers are the root, the Vedas are the branches, and his religious duties are the leaves. So guard the root with care; once the root is cut, there are no branches and no leaves.

first: माता च कमला देवी पिता देवो जनार्दनः ।
en: For one whose mother is the goddess Lakshmi, whose father is Lord Vishnu, and whose relatives are devotees of Vishnu, all three worlds are home.
Birds of many colours sit together on one tree, and at dawn they fly off in all ten directions; why grieve over that?

first: बुद्धिर् यस्य बलं तस्य निर्बुद्धेश् च कुतो बलम् ।
en: Whoever has intelligence has strength; how can a fool have strength? In the forest, a rabbit brought down an elephant mad with rage.

first: का चिन्ता मम जीवने यदि हरिर् विश्वंभरो गीयते ।
en: Why should I worry about my life, when Hari is praised as the one who feeds the world? If not, how would milk flow from a mother's breast for her baby? Thinking this again and again, Lord of the Yadus, Lord of Lakshmi, I spend my time only in serving your lotus feet.
Though I am skilled in the language of the gods, I still long for other languages, just as the gods, though they have nectar, still delight in the lips of heavenly maidens.
Flour is ten times more nourishing than grain, milk ten times more than flour, meat eight times more than milk, and ghee ten times more than meat.

first: शाकेन रोगा वर्ध्दते पयसो वर्ध्दते तनुः ।
en: Vegetables increase disease, milk builds the body, ghee increases vigour, and meat increases flesh.
